import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_71/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_71/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_71_0 and Source3_71_1 on 'city'
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="city", how="inner")

# Group by city and type, aggregate average fare
grouped = joined.groupby(["city", "type"], as_index=False)["fare"].mean()

# Ensure column types match target schema
grouped["city"] = grouped["city"].astype(str)
grouped["type"] = grouped["type"].astype(str)
grouped["fare"] = grouped["fare"].astype(float)

# Rename columns to match target schema (already matching)
Target3_71 = grouped[["city", "type", "fare"]]

# Write the result to the specified path
Target3_71.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_71/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_71/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_71/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on city column (inner join to keep only matching cities)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', left_on='city', right_on='city')

# Group by city and type (leftmost non-float unique attributes in target schema)
# Aggregate fare by average
result = joined.groupby(['city', 'type'], as_index=False).agg({'fare': 'mean'})

# Write output with exact target schema column names
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_71/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
